reviews.review:
It's very easy to just look past this in favor of its new, more modern younger brother, but ROR1 should not be overlooked, and I think differs a lot as well as exceeds ROR2 in many aspects.

GAMEPLAY: ROR1 does a great job of holding back, where ROR2 fails to do that. No item is too good, no enemy kills you too fast, no character is too complicated. It's a much more grounded experience where you really get to know your items, your tools, and your enemy. Enemies generally have a lot of health, meaning playing into all of your strengths and avoiding those of your enemies is proportionally rewarded, which feels great even if you may just be scraping by with some utility items. Unless you're chasing the high of seeing a lot of big numbers on your screen, it always feels better to outplay a wave of enemies than to just kill it before it attacks you, so if that's your thing ROR1 does that great.

SETTING/LORE: Just like ROR2, petrichor V is a great setting, and the logbook is a great tool for reading into almost everything about the game. The logs aren't as fleshed out as ROR2 but they're still a fun distraction and worth reading. The backgrounds are fantastic at making you feel incredibly small as well as the environments being interesting and different from each other.

JANK: This game buggy as hell. It's older and made when hopoo was less experienced so naturally it has more bugs than its polished sequel but ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. As well as that, items don't quite interact with each other like they do in ROR2, so expect that if bugs are a dealbreaker for you (but they shouldn't be).

TL;DR AND RATING OUT OF 10: I personally enjoy this game more than ROR2 (even if my hours don't reflect that I promise its just because of multiplayer) due to its more cohesive and honest mechanics. The second game is more likely more fun in general but this is seriously a banger of a game that shouldn't be reduced to "2D Risk of Rain 2".

8/10

Most of the time I've played this game has been trying to find the fun. The most fun I found was items that did all the work, and it definitely doesn't last.

The physical space you occupy is only 2D in appearance, in reality your gameplay takes place on a 1-dimensional line. You can attack left, or right. Jumping is just a way to temporarily move yourself off the line in which all fighting takes place.

The attacks you use in combat feel pitiful and inadequate. Starting with commando, you will have to get used to holding down the "z" key and waiting for health bars to drop to zero, or running away when the health bar won't drop to zero fast enough. Occasionally, you'll even press another two buttons to speed up your attacks even more! 
Of course you also have a dodge, but the dodge can only be used once every four seconds, making it's use about dodging 'big' attacks rather than.. most of the attacks. Not about maintaining aggression, just a get out of jail card when sponging up hits is too risky.

Items are essentially a requirement to keep up with ever-increasing enemy health bars and damage, and are an actual requirement to get certain unlocks, but items are offered almost entirely randomly. (There is an unlockable that lets you solve this issue, but it feels like cheating). As a result, most forms of progression feel like gambling, just instead of putting money into it, you're putting time into it.

All of this to say is, the game isn't challenging. It's just arbitrarily mean.

Buuuut
The art is pretty alright
And the stage tracks are all bangers.

UI is still clunky and achievements are still buged, but the game is extremely good. If it came out today as a side dish to the RoR2 - we would all applaud. I think it stood the test of time and claimed its rightful place as one of the "must-plays" in the genre. Easy recommend.
